title: WhatsApp Pricing 2026: Per-Message Rates by Country
summary: WhatsApp pricing offers no plans or charges—the app is completely free for all users with unlimited access to messages and calls.
body_markdown:
## What the Business Platform costs at realistic volumes


Depending on where the recipient lives, the marketing slice of your messages costs anywhere from about one US cent to nearly fourteen, and that slice is most of your bill.


**Since July 2025 Meta charges per delivered message** , so **a message that never arrives costs nothing** .


### Find your country's WhatsApp rate card


Open Meta's Business Platform pricing page, download the rate card and pick your billing currency. Then find the recipient's country, not your own, and read the category column: marketing, utility or authentication.


According to[Gupshup](https://www.gupshup.ai/resources/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/USD_Oct2025.pdf) , Germany costs $0.1365, the UK $0.0635, Brazil $0.0625, Indonesia $0.0411, the US $0.025 and India $0.0107, which means sending a message to Germany costs roughly 13 times more than to India.


Germany is roughly thirteen times India. The same campaign can cost an order of magnitude more purely because of where your customers live.


### Step 2: Count messages by category, not in total


Your actual costs depend on how your message distribution differs from this model.


Nobody pays per message for service replies, the ones answering a customer who wrote first. So in this mix I price only the 40% marketing share, leaving the other 60% unpriced. Your total bill will also include charges for utility and authentication messages.


### Worked monthly WhatsApp API cost examples


Take 10,000 messages a month in that mix. That's 4,000 marketing messages. Priced at the rates above:


Recipient country Rate per marketing message Monthly marketing cost


US $0.025 $100


UK $0.0635 $254


Germany $0.1365 $546


**More than five times as much** : that is what the same volume costs in Germany compared with the US. Utility and authentication messages add to each total at their own rates, which you read from the same card. Your provider's markup comes on top.


If your rate card discounts higher volumes, you're unlikely to feel it at 10,000 messages a month. Until your volume climbs, country and category will move your bill far more than tiers will.


Whatever connects your CRM to the Platform adds a meter of its own to this stack, and that meter decides whether good habits cost extra.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) charges 1 credit per flow run however many steps it has, so the flow above, with its reply log and category counter, costs what a bare template send costs.


Zapier's per-task billing and Make's per-module billing, both on their pricing pages, charge for each of those steps, which taxes you for splitting the work into small, checkable integrations.
